data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's mechanism conflates heterogeneity with decentralization: the stochastic firewalls it credits to 'intentional inefficiency' are a property of diversity, not of being small or independently operated. A single large service can deploy heterogeneous library versions and non-standard configurations across its internally redundant replicas, defeating global exploit propagation without any decentralization at all. Thus the argument fails to support the claim that a decentralized network is more resilient than one large service with strictly more internal redundancy; it only supports a 'diversity > homogeneity' thesis that is orthogonal to the decentralization-vs-centralization axis the problem asks about.
